assessments.reasoning: Printed p. 33 supports value-in and final value-out for a fixed formal with a corresponding assignable calling argument, explicitly describing the value at execution of return. The same page permits a variadic trailing formal to be rw and says the extra arguments are gathered into a tuple assigned to that formal. The frozen condition does not exclude that case. Printed p. 32 describes a fall-through return but does not separately state the rw transmission rule for fall-through.

challenge.method: Checked the ordinary declaration, explicit and implicit returns, rd and wr, assignable argument syntax, and the trailing starred rw form in the immediately following paragraph. Considered a starred rw formal called with two assignable variables.
challenge.results: For the variadic case the documented initial formal value is one tuple of the trailing arguments, while the frozen statement describes a one-to-one transfer involving an argument. The source offers no matching one-to-one writeback rule under that broad condition. A scope confined to one fixed non-variadic formal and an explicit return is directly supported. Aliasing and writeback ordering remain open.

limitations: The fixed-formal support does not qualify the frozen claim. The cited chapter leaves variadic writeback, simultaneous aliases, writeback order, and transmission on fall-through outside the directly stated fixed-formal rule.
